items_missed: No 'How are you today?' rapport opener, no agenda-setting statement ('I'll gather some details, then walk you through pricing... sound good?'), and no explicit 'sound good?' confirmation before jumping straight into address verification.
Never confirmed the customer's desired move date — jumped straight to offering Sunday, August 9th availability without first checking what date he actually needed.
Zip codes for both addresses were never confirmed — only street addresses were reviewed off the quote form.
Packing needs, storage stops, additional stops, and moving stressors were never probed.

Stairs and walk distance (both gathered earlier in the call) were never tied back in as time-estimate variables during the pricing/estimate walkthrough, and no equivalents (e.g., school bus reference) were used to make the estimate concrete.

Save Your Ass prep speech hit the core 'less prep time = lower bill' message and closed with a sense-check, but skipped concrete consolidation examples (loose items in drawers, garage/closet items, wall photos) and the 'take a carload' tip.
Didn't explicitly ask 'Any other questions before I let you go?' and never gave business hours or a direct way to reach the office outside of the confirmation email.
Customer's name (Rory) was never used once during the entire 9.8-minute call, despite being collected right at the start.

Speech clarity is a concern — the transcript is heavily garbled throughout (e.g., 'Ninette moving' for Einstein Moving, 'sterle fees' for transportation fees, 'bunds' for bands, 'cheese deep driveway' for narrow driveway/low-hanging trees), which is either an ASR artifact or a real articulation/pace issue — recommend an audio check either way.

No humor or rapport-building moments; the 60 cent/lb insurance valuation baseline was never mentioned alongside the No Worries Damage Coverage explanation; no proactive FAQ-answering beyond the standard script.
top_strength: The pricing/differentiators section was flawless — a clean 'super simple' pricing walkthrough covering the hourly rate, full inclusions, No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, and the complete no-hidden-fees pitch, paired with a math-accurate estimate ($525.35-$735 lines up exactly with 2.5-3.5 hrs at $105/hr x 2 movers) and a same-call booking with a clear bolded-email handoff.
coaching_note: The pricing pitch itself is close to rubric-perfect — the real gap is the rapport layer around it. Roselyn never used Rory's name once in almost 10 minutes, skipped the agenda-opener and 'how are you today,' and closed the Save Your Ass speech without the concrete consolidation examples or carload tip that actually change customer prep behavior. None of that costs the sale on an easy one-bedroom move, but on a harder or more anxious customer it's the difference between a transactional booking and a relationship — worth a quick coaching pass with Tetet on name-use habits and finishing the prep speech.
phone_presence_notes: Efficient and accurate, but almost entirely transactional — no use of the customer's name, no humor or rapport, and mechanical topic-to-topic transitions throughout; the only warmth markers are a couple of stock 'no problem'/'no worries' phrases.
audio_review_reason: Phone presence score is 2 (Flat), which the rubric flags for audio review on its own, and the transcript is unusually garbled throughout (repeated ASR-looking errors like 'Ninette moving,' 'sterle fees,' 'bunds,' 'cheese deep driveway'), making it unreliable to judge actual vocal tone/clarity from text alone — recommend pulling the real recording before finalizing the flat rating.
